description: Vantaan kaupunki järjestää tarjouskilpailun Vantaan asukaslehden painotyön ja jakelun hankinnasta. Optiona palveluntarjoaja voi tarjota telineitä, joissa lehden voi ottaa omatoimisesti asiakaspalvelupisteissä. Asukaslehti on Vantaan kaupungin julkaisema viranomaistiedote, jonka pitäisi tavoittaa kaikki kotitaloudet. Lehti on tuotettu sisällöllisesti kaupungin viestinnässä. Kilpailutuksessa ovat mukana painatus ja jakelu, mutta myös uudenlaisia tuotantomalleja harkitaan ennen kilpailutuksen aloittamista. Nykyisen paperikoko on leikattu tabloidi, mutta vaihtoehtona mukana kilpailussa on myös aikakausilehden paperikoko. Tavoitteena asukaslehden olisi tärkeä erottua erityisesti ilmaisjakeluna jaettavasta Vantaan Sanomista sekä muista paikallislehdistä. Hankinta koostuu Vantaan kaupungin asukaslehden nelivärisen painetun lehden rotaatiopainotyöstä sekä osoitteettomasta jakelusta. Lehdestä painetaan vuositasolla 2–4 eri laajuista (20–48 sivua) julkaisua. Jakelu koskee kaikkia sopimuskaudella Vantaan kuntarajojen sisäpuolella sijaitsevia kotitalouksia ja Vantaan kaupungin virastoja, laitoksia ja asiakaspalvelupisteitä. Jakelu toteutetaan osoitteettomana jakeluna. Tarkemmat painotyötä sekä jakelua koskevat tekniset vaatimukset löytyvät tarjouspyynnön liitteestä 2 Tekniset vaatimukset. Sopimus solmitaan yhden toimittajan kanssa, joka vastaa hankinnan kohteena olevan kokonaisuuden tuottamisesta. Tarkempi päivä ensimmäiselle painotyölle ja jakelulle sovitaan sopimuksentekovaiheessa. Jakelu tapahtuu etukäteen sovittuna viikonpäivinä. Sopimus on kestoltaan 24 kuukautta ja sopimusta voidaan jatkaa kahdella yhden vuoden optiolla.

title: Institutional Strengthening and Capability Development Plan for Disaster Risk Management in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
description: DAI Global UK is seeking a firm to prepare an Institutional Strengthening and Capability Development Plan for Disaster Risk Management (DRM) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), Pakistan. The assignment is delivered under Building Resilience and Addressing Vulnerability to Emergencies - Institutional Strengthening (BRAVE-IS), a multi-year (2026-2029) technical assistance programme funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO). The contracting organisation is DAI Pakistan Pvt. Ltd. The firm will work with the Relief, Rehabilitation and Settlement Department, Government of KP, and its attached agencies: the Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA), Rescue 1122 and the Civil Defence Directorate. The work is in four stages: - Stage 1, Inception (weeks 1-2) - Stage 2, Diagnostic and validation (weeks 3-6): institutional, financial, HR and digital systems assessment - Stage 3, Recommendations and plans (weeks 7-12): a five-year Institutional Strengthening Plan for each of PDMA, Rescue 1122 and Civil Defence - Stage 4, Early implementation support (weeks 13-36): implementation-ready products, commissioned at BRAVE-IS's discretion on completion of Stage 3 The contract is fixed price, with payment linked to acceptance of agreed deliverables. Personnel will be based in Peshawar, with field visits to selected districts of KP. The firm must propose four Key Persons: a Team Lead (institutional strengthening), a Public Financial Management Expert, a Digital Systems and ERP Expert, and a DRM Expert. HR management and GIS expertise are also required. How to apply The full Request for Proposals (RFP) is attached to this notice. Submit one email to brave-is@dai.com with the subject "BRAVE-IS-002 - Proposal - [Firm name]", attaching two PDFs: (i) the technical submission, with CVs as an annex, and (ii) the financial proposal, with separate budgets for Stages 1-3 and Stage 4. Clarification questions must be sent to brave-is@dai.com by 26 October 2026, with the subject "BRAVE-IS-002 - Clarification Question - [Firm name]". Responses will be shared with all bidders without identifying who asked. Proposals are due by 17:00 Pakistan Standard Time (12:00 UK time) on 4 November 2026 and must remain valid for 90 days. Late submissions will not be considered. Issue of this RFP does not commit DAI to award a contract.

title: Cattle Run Proposers Day Announcement
description: PROPOSERS DAY: DARPA is hosting a Proposers Day in support of DARPA-SN-27-03 Cattle Run program on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at the DARPA Conference Center (675 North Randolph Street, Arlington, VA 22203) from 8:00am to 5:00pm EST. The purpose of this conference is to provide information on the Cattle Run program; promote additional discussion on this topic; address questions from potential proposers; and provide a forum for potential proposers to meet for teaming opportunities. PROGRAM OBJECTIVE AND DESCRIPTION: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Cattle Run program enables cost effective cislunar constellations by developing and demonstrating autonomous spacecraft that leverage renewable propulsion [EF1.1]for persistent cislunar access. Phase 1 develops and rapidly launches a[SK2.1] Demonstrator spacecraf[SK3.1]t in 18 months that shows the ability of renewable propulsion to achieve sufficient acceleration, accurate vehicle control, and autonomous navigation necessary for persistent cislunar access. The Phase 1 objective is to collect on-orbit data to prove the performance of the renewable propulsion approach including vehicle control and navigation data. The Demonstrator spacecraft is launched below GEO and is agnostic of formfactor. Phase 2 creates multiple spacecraft and demonstrates persistent cislunar access.

title: Snow Removal and Ice Control, Debert & Surrounding Locations, CFB Halifax, NS
description: DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) – Project No. HX590822_87640 – Snow Removal and Ice Control, Debert and Surrounding Area, CFB Halifax, NS The work includes, but is not necessarily limited to, the supply of labour, material, supervision, and equipment necessary for Debert, Nova Scotia and surrounding areas. This includes Truro Armouries, Debert Rifle Range, Great Village, Masstown RX Site, Pictou Armoury, Springhill Armoury and Amherst Armoury NOTE: There is no site visit scheduled for this opportunity. The estimated value for the initial term of this opportunity is in the order of $293,150.00, with the option to extend for two additional one-year periods at an estimated value of $ $293,150.00 per year for a total estimated value of $879,450.00. This contract will be in place from date of award to April 30, 2027. description: Advance Procurement Notice National Supply and InStall Electronic Security Systems Source List Across Canada (Facility security clearance (FSC) SECRET) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at various locations across Canada (excluding Nunavut). The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential National Source List, which will include security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this Source List (SL) will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Description of the Project and Services As custodian of over 21,000 buildings across Canada, DND requires the deployment and maintenance of Electronic Security System at many locations. This solicitation proposes to establish a Security Installer Supplier Services source list to deliver the activities required to meet DND objectives. The services required are the supply, installation, verification, inspection, testing of electronic security system components and systems. The provision of training and maintenance support for the new and existing systems is also required. It is anticipated that the following solicitation will select multiple contractors, who will be placed on a National Source List with DCC to provide services on an “as and when required” basis to a maximum estimated value of $3,000,000.00, for a period of three (3) years from the date of establishment. At DCC sole discretion, the SL may be extended for up to two (2) additional two-year periods and increased in by up to $2,000,000 twice at any time. For better clarity, the total potential duration of the SL is seven (7) years, and the maximum potential value is $7,000,000. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. Contract Number: HOSL2501_83569 Title: National Supply and Install Electronic Security Systems Source List Approximate Estimate: $3,000,000 Anticipated Posting: November 2026 Source list establishment and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for selection on this SL, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Facility Security Clearance (FSC) at the level of SECRET, Document Safeguarding Capability at the level of SECRET, and the level of SECRET for personnel, issued by the Canadian Industrial Security Directorate (CISD), Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC). Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants or contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number 83569; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants or contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant or contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (Contract number listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and has submitted a proposal or a bid DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or bidder regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent or bidder will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent or bidder agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. description: *Please note that the ISC website will be available on September 23, 2026* ***AMENDMENT 001 - An attachment has been added. The document contains questions and answers related to the Challenge.*** ***AMENDMENT 002 - An attachment has been added. The document is to extend the solicitation closing date from 2026-10-21 to 2026-11-04.*** This Challenge Notice is issued under the Innovative Solutions Canada Program (ISC) Call for Proposals 004 (EN578-24ISC4). For general ISC information, Offerors can visit the ISC website at: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en Please refer to the Solicitation Documents Innovative Solutions Canada Program Call for Proposals – 004 - Tender Notice | CanadaBuys https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 which contains the process for submitting a proposal. Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/minerva-initiative-uncrewed-aircraft-system-deconfliction Challenge title: MINERVA Initiative – Uncrewed Aircraft System Deconfliction Challenge sponsor: Department of National Defense (DND) Funding Mechanism: Contract MAXIMUM CONTRACT VALUE: $500,000.00 CAD Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. Phase 2: - The maximum funding available for any Phase 2 contract resulting from this Challenge is : $500,000.00 CAD excluding applicable taxes, shipping, travel and living expenses, as required. - The maximum duration for any Phase 2 contract resulting from this Challenge is up to 15 months (excluding submission of the final report). - Estimated number of Phase 2 contracts: 5 This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to award any contract for the total approximate funding. Final decisions on the number of Phase 2 awards will be made by Canada on the basis of factors such as evaluation results, departmental priorities and availability of funds. Canada reserves the right to make partial awards and to negotiate project scope changes. Note: Selected companies are eligible to receive one contract per phase per challenge. Travel: Travel to Suffield, Alberta for prototype demonstration. Kick-off Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Progress Review Meeting(s): Any progress review meetings will be conducted by telephone or videoconference. Final Review Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Problem Statement: Challenge Statement Summary The challenge is to provide the Department of National Defense (DND) and the Canadian Army (CA) a software solution to provide an airspace common operating picture so that it can plan, deconflict, and control uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) traffic, including their use of the radio frequency (RF) spectrum, in order to ensure the safe and efficient management of UAS to enable the Canadian soldier to successfully fight and survive on the future battlefield. Details: Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Be Windows-based. 2. Allow a user to create and store flight plans, including radio frequency requirements. 3. Have a flight plan repository (database) that stores the 4D (3D + time) trajectories and spectrum requirements of all accepted flight plans. 4. Enable integration of supplemental data services such as crewed aircraft flight plans and weather. 5. Generate an optimal 4D flight path for UAS based on specific mission goals and physical limits. 6. Be able to check new flight requests against existing flight plans, airspace constraints (no-fly zones) and RF spectrum requests to detect conflicts and resolve them (via set priorities or a human decision). 7. Generate 4D blocks of deconflicted airspace (a "tunnel" or a "box") where a UAS is permitted to fly. Additional Outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Analyze real-time data from UASs to prevent collisions and automatically adjust flight paths for UASs in controlled airspace. 2. Check in real-time whether a UAS is following its pre-approved, deconflicted trajectory. 3. Demonstrate capacity in having its critical components produced and sourced in countries within the NATO alliance, NATO Partners or Major Non-NATO Allies. To achieve this, Offerors are requested to provide as an attachment to their proposal, a list identifying the solution's critical components, the country of production and sourcing for each component. Critical components and requested information for each Critical components are defined below: Critical components: 1. Radio 2. Ground control station (GCS) 3. On-board computer 4. Any software Requested information: i. Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM): Name of the original equipment manufacturer of the product being sourced ii. OEM URL: Provide the URL of the OEM iii. Software: Confirm if developed by Offeror or outsourced iv. Product name: Provide the OEM's product name v. Model number: Provide the OEM's model and/or version number of the product vi. Product URL: Provide the URL of the OEM product, model, and version vii. Country of origin IMPORTANT NOTE: For this challenge, kindly disregard the Attachment requirements detailed at Section D in the Web-Portal, and instead adhere to the following: - The attachment measures 8.5" by 11" with a maximum size of 10Mb. - Only the following formats will be accepted: JPG, GIF, TIF, PDF or PNG. - The attachment must be clear and legible. Note: Including an attachment is not mandatory, but forms part of the Additional Outcomes, which is scored up to 10 points. The Applicant (Offeror) acknowledges that it is within Canada's sole discretion to determine whether the attachment is removed or included in the Offer. Background & Context The CA is undergoing a generational modernization effort to address the evolving nature of technology, the changing character of conflict, and the unravelling of the geopolitical system. The transformative changes being made are conceptually described in the CA publication Inflection Point 2025. This document provides the broad context for modernization and directs the development and acquisition of key systems; in particular, it states: Key to this transformation is the integration of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, robotics, autonomous and uncrewed systems. These capabilities will support a wide range of functions, from intelligence analysis and predictive modeling to targeting and operational execution. The CA, in recognizing this need, has purchased foreign robotics and autonomous systems of varying quality and has identified challenges purchasing systems that meet operational requirements, in particular related to cold-weather operations, and that have stable supply chains. Further, purchases have, in the past, been constrained by limited manufacturing capacity of industry partners. To address this, the Government of Canada's recently released policy Canada's Defence Industrial Strategy, emphasizes the need to develop a strong domestic industrial capacity to produce defence materiel. This policy directs the CA to seek solutions to operational problems through Canadian industry, which will both improve the CA's capability while providing the foundation of a strong defence industrial base able to scale production of quality defence material. To date, engagements with Canadian industry have revealed a wide variety of small/medium companies that have commercial technologies that could, with support, be tailored to military requirements.

title: Stadtsicherung Bitterfeld: Erneuerung der Rohrleitungen zur Ableitung der Hebungswässer im Sicherungsbereich 9 (Friedhof)
description: In der Stadt Bitterfeld-Wolfen ist das Grundwasser durch die Einstellung des Braunkohletagebaus und das Ende der damit verbundenen Sümpfungsmaßnahmen sowie auch aufgrund anderer Einflüsse wieder angestiegen. Durch das aufgestiegene Grundwasser ergaben sich in den betroffenen Stadtteilen Bitterfelds Gefahren für Menschen, Natur und Sachgüter. Es wurden Sicherungsmaßnahmen zum Schutz von Gebäuden und Infrastruktur im Ortsteil Bitterfeld notwendig. Das Maßnahmenkonzept des Projektes Stadtsicherung zielt auf die Gewährleistung von ausreichenden Flurabständen des Grundwasserspiegels ab, um so eine Gefährdung der bestehenden Bebauung/ Nutzung zu verhindern. Dies erfolgt mit einer Kombination aus dem zielgerichteten Ausbau, der Bewirtschaftung und Unterhaltung der Wasser abführenden Fließgewässer, der Grundwasserabsenkung mittels Drainagen und Brunnen sowie mit baulichen Sicherungen einzelner Gebäude. In diesem Zusammenhang wurde im Rahmen des Maßnahmekonzeptes 2019 ff. für den Sicherungsbereich 9 - Friedhof abgeleitet, dass dieser mit einer Hebungsmenge von ca. 250.000 m³/a einen Schwerpunkt im Projekt Stadtsicherung darstellt. Nach derzeitigem Kenntnisstand (Friedhofsbelegung/ Liegedauer) ist die hydraulische Sicherung über 2 von 3 Grundwasserbrunnen aufgrund der aktuellen Belegungssituation ggf. bis ins Jahr 2043 erforderlich. Für die hydraulische Sicherung und Ableitung der gehobenen Grundwässer ist ein funktionstüchtiges/ leckagefreies Rohrleitungsnetz zwischen den in Betrieb befindlichen Brunnen und der Einleitstelle abfr (ins Gelbe Wasser) zwingend erforderlich. Gegenstand der Vergabe ist die Erneuerung/ Ertüchtigung der vorgenannten Rohrleitungen wie folgt: - Erd- und Schachtarbeiten im offenen Grabenverbau vom Haupt- bis zum Entlastungsschacht (ca. 192 m) sowie vom Hauptschacht zu den beiden Brunnen BrFr01 und BrFr02 (insgesamt ca. 110 m); die Rohrleitung BrFr02 bis BrFr03 ist nicht Bestandteil der Instandsetzung, da der BrFr03 nicht mehr in Betrieb ist - Austausch (Rückbau und Neuverlegung im vorhanden Rohrgraben) der Druckrohrleitungen inkl. Umschlussarbeiten und Einbindung in die bestehenden Schachtbauwerke gemäß den Vorgaben des AG - Entsorgung des alten Rohrleitungsmaterials sowie überschüssigen Aushubmaterials - Erneuerung vorhandener Schieber und/ oder Absperrventile im Leitungsverlauf _ Eine während der Arbeiten erforderliche Wasserhaltung für die im Dauerbetrieb befindlichen Brunnen BrFr01 und BrFr02 bis zur Einleitstelle abfr wird von MDSE installiert und betrieben. Auftraggeber (Vergabestelle) für die angefragten Leistungen ist die MDSE Mitteldeutsche Sanierungs- und Entsorgungsgesellschaft mbH als Projektträgerin des Projektes Stadtsicherung Bitterfeld. Die Zuschlagserteilung bzw. Beauftragung erfolgt von der MDSE.

title: Siviilipalveluskeskuksen pesulapalvelut 2027-
description: Siviilipalveluskeskuksen pesulapalvelut 2027- KEHA-keskus pyytää tarjoustanne Siviilipalveluskeskuksen pesulapalvelujen tuottamisesta. Siviilipalveluskeskuksen pesulapalvelu sisältää siviilipalvelusvelvollisten käytössä olevien liinavaatteiden noudon, pesun, kuivauksen, mankeloinnin sekä palautuksen. Liinavaatteisiin kuuluvat tyynyliinat, aluslakanat, pussilakanat ja käsipyyhkeet. Sopimuksen perusteella voidaan tarvittaessa tilata vastaavia pesulapalveluja myös tyynyjen, peittojen sekä muiden Siviilipalveluskeskuksessa käytettävien tekstiilien, kuten verhojen ja työvaatteiden, pesuun. Kaikki tekstiilit pestään niiden omien pesuohjeiden mukaisesti. Palveluntarjoaja toimittaa pyykin kuljetuksessa tarvittavat nouto- ja palautuspussit sekä rullakot tai muut kuljetusvälineet. Puhdas pyykki tulee palauttaa pusseihin tai muihin kuljetusvälineisiin pakattuna ja tekstiilityypeittäin lajiteltuna siten, että eri tekstiililajit ovat erikseen pakattuina. Pesuun toimitettavan pyykin pakkaamisesta vastaa Siviilipalveluskeskus. Likapyykkiä ei lajitella tekstiilityypeittäin ennen kuljetusta, vaan lajittelu tapahtuu pesulassa. Liinavaatteet noudetaan ja puhtaat tekstiilit palautetaan perjantaisin klo 12.00–16.00. Nouto- ja palautus tapahtuvat 1–2 viikon välein riippuen Siviilipalveluskeskuksen kulloisestakin siviilipalvelusvelvollisten määrästä. Palveluntarjoaja punnitsee pyykin kuivapainoisena ennen pesua. Pyykin määrä on arviolta 50–300 kg viikossa, mutta yksittäisinä viikkoina määrä voi olla tätä suurempi tai pienempi. Ilmoitettu arvio ei sido tilaajaa, eikä palveluntarjoajalla ole oikeutta korvaukseen, mikäli pyykin määrä jää alle 300 kilogramman viikossa tai pyykkiä ei ole lainkaan. Palveluntarjoajan tulee nimetä sopimusasioista vastaava yhteyshenkilö sekä pesulatoiminnasta vastaava henkilö. Tehtävät voidaan osoittaa samalle henkilölle tai eri henkilöille. Yhteistyöpalavereita järjestetään tarvittaessa. Laskuilla tulee eritellä liinavaatteiden pesupalvelut ja muiden tekstiilien pesupalvelut erikseen. Sopimus tulee voimaan 1.1.2027 ja on voimassa toistaiseksi.,

title: Netherlands – Bicycles – EA Bedrijfsfietsen en handhavingsfietsen Gemeente Zwolle
description: De gemeente Zwolle sluit voor deze opdracht per perceel een Raamovereenkomst met één Opdrachtnemer. De Raamovereenkomsten hebben betrekking op de levering van fietsen in eigendom van de gemeente en het bijbehorende onderhoud, reparatie en service. Lease- en huurconstructies maken geen onderdeel uit van deze aanbesteding. De aanbesteding bestaat uit twee afzonderlijk te gunnen percelen: Perceel 1 – Handhavingsfietsen Dit perceel betreft de levering van handhavingsfietsen, waaronder robuuste fietsen zoals mountainbikes en elektrische varianten, die worden ingezet bij de uitvoering van toezicht- en handhavingstaken. Perceel 2 – Bedrijfsfietsen Dit perceel betreft de levering van elektrische en niet-elektrische bedrijfsfietsen. Deze fietsen worden ingezet als functioneel vervoermiddel ter ondersteuning van de dagelijkse werkzaamheden, met name voor korte dienstreizen en verplaatsingen tussen locaties. Omvang Perceel 1 – Handhavingsfietsen De geraamde opdrachtwaarde bedraagt € 156.392, - exclusief btw over de maximale looptijd van vier jaar. Om beperkte volumewijzigingen gedurende de looptijd te kunnen opvangen, wordt voor de reguliere scope een maximale opdrachtwaarde van € 195.490, - exclusief btw gehanteerd. Daarnaast is de volgende herzieningsmogelijkheid voorzien: Uitbreiding handhavingsfietsen: als gevolg van personele wijzigingen, veranderingen in mobiliteitsbeleid of organisatorische verschuivingen kan sprake zijn van uitbreiding met maximaal tien (10) handhavingsfietsen. De maximale financiële omvang van deze uitbreiding bedraagt € 56.000, - exclusief btw, bestaande uit maximaal € 50.000, - voor aanschaf en € 6.000, - voor onderdelen en onderhoud. Daarmee bedraagt de maximale financiële omvang voor Perceel 1 inclusief deze herzieningsmogelijkheid € 251.490, - exclusief btw. Omvang Perceel 2 – Bedrijfsfietsen De geraamde opdrachtwaarde bedraagt € 292.916, - exclusief btw over de maximale looptijd van vier jaar. Om beperkte volumewijzigingen gedurende de looptijd te kunnen opvangen, wordt voor de reguliere scope een maximale opdrachtwaarde van € 366.145, - exclusief btw gehanteerd. Daarnaast zijn de volgende herzieningsmogelijkheden voorzien: Uitbreiding elektrische bedrijfsfietsen: bij vervanging van reguliere bedrijfsfietsen kan gedurende de looptijd worden gekozen voor uitbreiding met maximaal vijftien (15) elektrische bedrijfsfietsen. De maximale financiële omvang hiervan bedraagt € 67.200, - exclusief btw, bestaande uit maximaal € 36.000, - voor aanschaf en € 31.200, - voor onderdelen en onderhoud. Uitbreiding elektrische bedrijfsfietsen in verband met dienstreizen: als gevolg van gewijzigd mobiliteitsbeleid kan voor een groep medewerkers behoefte ontstaan aan aanvullende elektrische fietsen. Hiervoor kan de vloot worden uitgebreid met maximaal twintig (20) elektrische bedrijfsfietsen. De maximale financiële omvang van deze uitbreiding bedraagt € 104.000, - exclusief btw. Daarmee bedraagt de maximale financiële omvang voor Perceel 2 inclusief deze herzieningsmogelijkheden € 537.345, - exclusief btw. De totale maximale financiële omvang van beide percelen gezamenlijk bedraagt daarmee € 788.835, - exclusief btw. De betreffende Raamovereenkomst eindigt uiterlijk na afloop van de maximale contractduur of eerder wanneer de voor het betreffende perceel geldende maximale opdrachtwaarde is bereikt.

title: Germany – Demolition work – VE8309HB - Rückbau im Bereich des VKN München
description: Gegenstand der Maßnahme ist der Schadstoffsanierung, Entkernung und Abbruch im Bereich des Verkehrsknotenpunktes (VKN) Hbf München. Für die Herstellung der Vorhaltemaßnahme U9 und des Neubau Empfangsgebäudes sollen die daran angrenzenden Bereiche (Durchgangshalle sowie Nord- und Südbau) abgebrochen werden. Die Abbruchmaßnahmen umfassen die oberirdischen Teile der beschriebenen Gebäudeteile wie auch die bestehenden Untergeschosse und somit die kompletten Bauwerke, inkl. aller Medien / Versorgungsanlagen. Weiterhin werden in den jeweiligen Abbruchphasen die öffentlichen Wege vom Baufeld abgetrennt. Die notwendige bauliche Abtrennung des Querbahnsteigs vom Baufeld ist zu realisieren.

title: France – Technical control services – PRESTATIONS DE CONTROLES PERIODIQUES ET PONCTUELS DES EQUIPEMENTS DE LA REGIE DES TRANSPORTS METROPOLITAINS (4 LOTS)
description: 1/ La consultation est décomposée en quatre lots ci-après énoncés : Lot 1 Contrôles périodiques et ponctuels des appareils de levage et monte-charges non accessibles ; Lot 2 Contrôles périodiques et ponctuels des installations électriques ; Lot 3 : Contrôles périodiques et ponctuels des escaliers mécaniques, ascenseurs et monte-charges accessibles ; Lot 4 : Contrôles périodiques et ponctuels des équipements sous pression. Les prestations à réaliser sont décrites et s'exécutent conformément aux dispositions du CCAP ainsi que du CCTP communs à tous les lots, documents joints en annexe du présent Avis d'appel public à la concurrence (AAPC). Les candidats ont la possibilité de soumissionner à un, plusieurs ou à la totalité des lots. Les offres seront examinées lot par lot. Les candidats ne peuvent présenter des offres variables selon le nombre de lots susceptibles d'être obtenus. Chaque lot donne lieu à la passation d'un marché séparé. 2/ Les présents marchés publics sont passés selon une procédure avec négociation, en application des articles L21243, R21244 et R216121 à R216123 du Code de la commande publique. Chaque accord-cadre est conclu avec un seul opérateur économique et exécuté en partie par l'émission de bons de commande, pour les prestations décrites dans les documents contractuels (dans les conditions fixées aux articles R2162-13 et R2162-14 du Code) et en partie par la conclusion de marchés subséquents pour les besoins dont toutes les stipulations contractuelles ne sont pas fixées dans les documents de l'accord-cadre (conformément aux articles R2162-7, R2162-11 et R2162-12 du Code). En application de l'article R2162-4 du Code, les marchés publics sont conclus sans montant minimum d'engagement et avec un montant maximum d'engagement sur leur durée initiale d'un an, à savoir : Lot 1 : 220 000,00 euros HT ; Lot 2 : 250 000,00 euros HT ; Lot 3 : 70 000,00 euros HT ; Lot 4 : 20 000,00 euros HT. 3/ Il s'agit de marchés publics de services qui se réfèrent au Cahier des Clauses Administratives Générales applicable aux marchés publics de fournitures courantes et de services (CCAG/FCS), approuvé par l'arrêté du 30 mars 2021. 4/ Au stade des candidatures, les documents transmis avec l'Avis d'Appel Public à la Concurrence (AAPC), figurent dans le Règlement de la consultation « Phase candidature », joint en annexe de l'AAPC. 5/ Les candidats doivent obligatoirement transmettre leur candidature (et leur offre en phase ultérieure) de façon dématérialisée via le sitewww.achatpublic.com. 6/ La RTM mettra à disposition le Dossier de Consultation des Entreprises (DCE) complet aux candidats admis à déposer une offre, via le site www.achatpublic.com qui fournira à ces derniers les modalités de téléchargement. Les candidats devront transmettre leur offre obligatoirement de façon dématérialisée via le site Internet achatpublic.com. 7/ En phase ultérieure, chaque candidat a l'obligation de visiter certains lieux dans lesquels il sera amené à intervenir, afin de mieux appréhender les conditions d'exécution des prestations. Les modalités pour effectuer la visite seront précisées dans l'Invitation à Soumissionner (IS), document constitutif du Dossier de Consultation des Entreprises (DCE), qui sera transmis aux candidats admis à déposer une offre.

title: Snow removal, de-icing, and related winter maintenance services
description: U.S. Embassy Bucharest, Romania, requests quotations from qualified contractors to provide snow removal, de-icing, and related winter maintenance services at designated Embassy facilities and residences. The Government intends to establish an IDIQ contract under which services may be ordered as needed during each defined winter-season service window. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, supervision, equipment, tools, fuel, personal protective equipment, transportation, insurance, management, and other resources necessary to perform the services, except materials or equipment expressly identified as Government-furnished in the Statement of Work (SOW). This is a fixed-price contract for snow removal and cleaning services for the U.S. Embassy Bucharest. The Government will pay the Contractor the fixed price per hour for standard services that will be satisfactorily performed.

title: FPC BRYAN, TX - REPLACE HVAC SYSTEM ICC BUILDING
description: Notice of Combined Synopsis/Solicitation This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the applicable Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 procedures. This announcement constitutes the solicitation; quotations are requested, and no separate written solicitation will be issued beyond the RFQ documents included in this posting. This acquisition is a 100% total small business set-aside. The solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference and in full text as provided in Attachment 2. The current text of Federal Acquisition Regulation provisions and clauses is available at https://www.acquisition.gov/. Requirement The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Prison Camp - Bryan, seeks a responsible small business to supply and deliver two (2) 25-ton single-packaged air-conditioning units with gas heat, 208/230V, three-phase, 60 Hz, for Government installation at the ICC Building. This is a supply-and-delivery-only acquisition; installation is not included. Equipment and materials shall conform to Attachment 3, Statement of Work/Specifications. Quotations shall identify the manufacturer and model of the proposed units and include complete manufacturer product data sheets and specifications demonstrating compliance with the SOW. The Government-approved SOW controls the technical requirement. Delivery destination: Federal Bureau of Prisons, FPC Bryan, 1100 Ursuline Avenue, Bryan, TX 77803. Deliveries may be received Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., excluding Federal holidays, as stated in the SOW. FOB destination. Quoters shall expressly provide their proposed delivery date. Acquisition and quotation requirements NAICS: 333415 (size standard shown in Attachment 2: 1,250 employees). Product Service Code: 4120. Contract type: firm-fixed-price. Vendors shall submit a completed SF 1449 (Attachment 2), firm-fixed unit and extended prices for both units including delivery, manufacturer/model identification, complete technical literature, and a proposed delivery date. Vendors must satisfy applicable small business eligibility requirements, including any applicable nonmanufacturer rule. Quotations shall be emailed to r3phillips@bop.gov. Faxed and hand-delivered quotations will not be accepted. The quotation email subject should identify RFQ 15B50427Q00000001. Questions shall be submitted in writing to the same email address. Any material clarification or change will be published as an amendment on SAM.gov. Quoters are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for amendments. Quotation deadline: November 4, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. Eastern Time Questions deadline: October 29, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. Eastern Time Basis for award The Government intends to make one firm-fixed-price award to the responsible, eligible small business whose quotation represents the best value to the Government, considering (1) Technical Acceptability, (2) Delivery Schedule, and (3) Price. Technical compliance will be evaluated against the SOW based on submitted manufacturer literature. Delivery will be evaluated against the quoter�s proposed schedule; an earlier achievable delivery date may provide additional value. Technical Acceptability and Delivery Schedule, combined, are more important than Price. The Government may select a higher-priced quotation where documented technical or delivery benefits justify the premium, or a lower-priced quotation when such benefits do not justify additional cost. The Government may make award without discussions. Registration, funding and payment Quoters must comply with the SAM.gov registration and representation requirements applicable to this solicitation and award. The Government will verify registration, exclusions, responsibility, and small-business eligibility before award. Issuance of this RFQ does not obligate the Government to make an award or reimburse quotation preparation costs. Payment will be made by electronic funds transfer in accordance with FAR 52.232-33, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer�System for Award Management. Solicitation documents and point of contact Attachment 1 � Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Notice and Quotation Instructions Attachment 2 � SF 1449 and Continuation Pages, Solicitation 15B50427Q00000001 Attachment 3 � Government-approved ICC Building HVAC Statement of Work/Specifications Contracting Officer: Ragan Phillips | r3phillips@bop.gov. All questions and communications before award must be directed to the Contracting Officer in writing via email. Only an authorized Contracting Officer may obligate the Government. title: Request for Information (RFI) - Drinking Water
description: FEDERAL EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT AGENCY (FEMA) REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) 10/15/2026 The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Logistics Management Division, Distribution Management Division, Supply Chain Integration Branch, seeks to identify and assess industry capabilities to provide disaster Water in support of emergency response and steady-state operations within the Continental United States (CONUS) and Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS). The information collected will be used to support contingency planning, requirements development, and operational readiness assessments during natural disasters, humanitarian assistance, and other emergency response scenarios. This RFI is issued solely for information gathering purposes to identify sources that can provide support for the Supply Chain Integration Branch. In accordance with FAR 15.101(e), RFIs may be used when the Government wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information, and capabilities for planning purposes. Responses to these RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their RFI response. Respondents will not receive additional information in response to their submittal to the RFI and will not be notified of the resulting market research. Respondents shall identify any proprietary information in its RFI response. Information submitted in response to this RFI will be used at the discretion of the Government. Further, the information submitted will remain confidential as permitted by law, including the Freedom of Information and Privacy Acts. FEMA reserves the right to utilize any non-proprietary technical information in the anticipated PWS or solicitation. Although it is not necessary to address in their response, respondents shall be aware of any potential, actual, or perceived organizational conflicts of interest. Any real or potential conflicts must be sufficiently mitigated prior to a contract award. For further guidance, refer to the Federal Acquisition Regulation, Part 9.5. NAICS CODE: 312112 Bottled Water Manufacturing industry Subject: IDIQ Water Recompete Request for Information (RFI) Interested contractors shall submit their RFI responses electronically to Oneko Dunbar, Contracting Officer, at Oneko.Dunbar@fema.dhs.gov and Marcia Irizarry-Snyder, Contract Specialist at Marcia.Irizarrysnyder@fema.dhs.gov no later than 11:00 am Eastern Time (ET) November 4, 2026. Questions regarding this RFI are due no later than 11:00 am ET October 20, 2026.

title: C1DA--AE Replace Roofing 539-25-101
description: Provide complete design services, including all necessary schematics, design development, surveys, cost estimates, construction drawings and specifications, and construction period services (CPS) for solicitation to replace and repair roofing and lighting protection at the Cincinnati VA Medical Center, 3200 Vine Street, Cincinnati, OH 45220 (Building Numbers: 1, 2, 3, 8, 13, 14, 15, 16 and trailers) and the Fort Thomas Campus, 1000 S. Ft. Thomas Ave, Ft. Thomas, KY 41075 (Building Numbers: 64, 117 and trailers), in accordance with the general items as written (231000 sq-ft - estimated). This project will replace and repair the roofing and lightning protection. Replacement of outdated roofing and lighting protection will reduce overall emergency maintenance, increase facility operation, and provide proper protection. SELECTION CRITERIA The Government will evaluate each potential contractor under the terms of its: A. Professional qualifications necessary for satisfactory performance of required services; B. Specialized experience and technical competence in the type of work required, including, where appropriate, experience in energy conservation, pollution prevention, waste reduction, and the use of recovered materials; C. Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time; D. Past performance on contracts with Government agencies and private industry in terms of cost control, quality of work, and compliance with performance schedules; E. Location in the general geographical area of the project and knowledge of the locality of the project; provided, that application of this criterion leaves an appropriate number of qualified firms, given the nature and size of the project; F. Experience in construction period services to include professional field inspections during the construction period, review of construction submittals, support in answering requests for information during the construction period, and support of construction contract changes to include drafting statements of work, and cost estimates shall be included as an evaluation criterion when construction period services is included in the statement of work for A-E services, and; G. The extent to which potential contractors identify and commit to the use of service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, veteran-owned small businesses, and other types of small businesses as subcontractors. SUBMITTAL INSTRUCTIONS All interested and capable contractors must submit an electronic copy of their SF 330s, via email, by the closing time/date of this announcement. Note the following: No hard/physical copies will be accepted. Limit SF 330 packages to 50 pages. Only the first 50 pages will be evaluated. Submit all documentation as one single file. The total size of the electronic submission (email and all attachments) must not exceed 15MB; larger emails may get rejected by the network server and will be considered non-responsive. Cited relevant projects must be within the last five (5) years. Submit packages via email to the contract specialist by the deadline:� ronald.heidemann@va.gov Subject line must include the notice number: 36C25027R0009 Please include your firm s POC and UEI in the email body. ***End of Presolicitation Notice**

title: Transport of slabs
description: This opportunity supports the delivery of the HS2 programme and involves the transportation of precast concrete slab-track units from the PACADAR UK factory to multiple locations along the HS2 route. The requirement is for approximately 12,000 slabs, equating to around 2,400 HGV loads, making it a significant logistics package with a consistent volume of work. Suppliers will be required to provide suitable HGV transport capable of safely carrying five slab units per load while complying with all relevant transport, safety and load restraint regulations. Deliveries will be made to various locations along the HS2 corridor, with loading at the factory and offloading at site undertaken by others. Interested suppliers will be asked to demonstrate their transport capability, available fleet capacity and proposed delivery approach, together with competitive commercial rates. Further information on the scope, delivery requirements, indicative volumes and pricing structure is available within the attached documentation.

title: IDIQ For Architect Engineer (A/E) Services for Central Office
description: THIS IS A SYNOPSIS OF PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION. FOLLOW THE INSTRUCTIONS CONTAINED IN THIS NOTICE FOR RESPONDING TO THIS OPPORTUNITY. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP), Central (CO), anticipates the need for indefinitedelivery indefinite-quantity (IDIQ), firm fixed-price contracts for supplemental architect-engineer (A-E) services, with a one (1) year base requirement and up to four (4) unilaterally exercised option years, with a possibility for a six-month extention as well. The Government is not obligated to exercise any of the option periods. While the Government anticipates multiple awards, no more than four (4) awards are expected. The services will be for various FBOP facilities throughout the United States. See the Statement of Work attachment for description of services. Most projects will take place in a fully occupied, fully operational, secure correctional environment. Most projects require complex design effort and detail along with extensive coordination between design disciplines, the institutions, and Central Office during design and construction. Firms are to perform services as required by the issuance of individual task orders. The guaranteed annual minimum amount of each contract is $10,000.00 and the estimated annual maximum is $10,000,000. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this requirement is 541310 (Architectural Services). Interested firms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://SAM.gov. This requirement will be fulfilled pursuant to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 36.6 and the Brooks Act. Pursuant to FAR Deviation 36.201(b), for any firm(s) receiving award under this requirement, no construction contract may be awarded to the firm (including any of its subsidiaries or affiliates) that designs the corresponding project Firms having the capabilities to perform the services described in this announcement are invited to respond by submitting Parts I and II of the Standard Form 330 (Architect Engineer Qualifications) dated not more than 12 months before the date of this synopsis. The current version of the form along with any extra pages/sections may be retrieved from www.gsa.gov/forms (Type in "SF330" in the Form Name or Number block for a full listing of the associated forms. *** Include a cover letter detailing your firms name and main office address (as registered in sam.gov), UEI#, Tax ID# (TIN), CAGE code, and main point of contact for your firm through out the solicitation process (phone and e-mail). Submissions should be on standard 8.5'' x 11" format. No extraneous attachments. Selection criteria will be based on the following evaluation factors in descending order of importance: Specialized Experience and Technical Competence (32%) Capacity to Accomplish the Work in the Required Time (demonstrated ability to complete projects on time) (27%) Acceptability of an Established Team of Key Personnel (23%) Professional Qualifications Necessary for Satisfactory Performance (including licensed engineers and architects licensed Nationwide)(18%) Submit details (maximum of one page per project) of not more than five significant and/or complex renovation projects completed in the past five years (Utilize Section F of the SF-330). Identify the lead designer and address the design approach with salient features for each project. Discuss how the client's program, function, image, mission, economic, schedule and operational objectives were satisfied by the overall design/planning solution. Include tangible evidence where possible such as certificates, awards, peer recognition, etc., demonstrating design excellence. Provide a client reference contact for each project, including name, title, address, phone, fax, and email. Submit resumes of key personnel outlining commitment to projects and qualifications and relevant experience as individuals and as a team. Highlight sustainability features incorporated into the project design (e.g., energy/water efficiency, waste reduction, use of recycled materials). Submit a narrative outline of not more than one page describing the firm's project management planning, coordination, scheduling and production facilities, capabilities, and techniques for both design and construction inspection (Utilize Section H of the SF-330). Submit a narrative outline (maximum one page) with examples describing the firm's ability to evaluate/develop accurate preliminary project budgets, ability to control project costs during design process, ability to design within funding limitations, methods used to coordinate construction documents, work of various engineering disciplines, and provide general production quality control (Utilize Section H of the SF-330). No fax or paper submissions. Submit electronically through the JEFS APP BOX at link below: https://jefs.app.box.com/f/336fbbe977394048827a238f901db3a3 All submissions should be in Adobe format. Title the file in the following format: 15BBNF26R70000006_ Company Name_SF330 Architect Engineer (A/E) Services for Central Office Electronic copies of each submission shall be compatible with the following software products: Adobe Acrobat Reader 11 and Microsoft Office Suite 2016. Narrative portions of the submission shall be in Adobe Acrobat portable document file (pdf) searchable text format. The Submitter shall not embed sound or video (e.g., MPEG) files into the submission files. Electronic files shall be clearly identified for each volume, section, and item. The Submitter must ensure electronic files are virus-free and shall run an anti-virus scan before submission. Submissions by mail or hand carried will not be evaluated. All responses must be received no later than Wednesday, November 4, 2026, 10:00 AM MST. It is the responsibility of the Submitter to confirm receipt by contacting Alex Jackson, Contracting Officer, at a4jackson@bop.gov. Failure to submit all required information may result in rejection. All submissions received after the exact time specified for receipt shall be treated as late submissions and will not be considered except under facts and circumstances allowed by the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR). Based on these submissions, a short-list of no more than six (6) firms will be selected for an interview. Firms should be prepared to discuss their submittals and to demonstrate their ability to fulfill the contract requirements. Final selection will be based on SF-330 submissions and interviews. After the SF-330 review and interview process, four (4) selected firms will be invited to submit a formal proposal and must be prepared to negotiate overhead, profit, and hourly rates for anticipated disciplines for use in negotiating firm-fixed-price contract rates as well as firm-fixed-price task orders to be completed under the contract. All contract awards and task orders thereunder are subject to a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. This acquisition is 100 percent small business set-aside. Firms must be registered in SAM.gov as a small business (see FAR provision 52.219-1 in the Representations & Certifications section of the SAM registration. If you have questions about SAM.gov, Government procurements in general, or need assistance in the preparation of your bid/proposal/offer, a local Procurement Technical Assistance Center (PTAC) may be able to help. The Procurement Technical Assistance Program was authorized by Congress in 1985 in an effort to expand the number of businesses capable of participating in the Government marketplace. To locate a PTAC near you, go to http://www.aptac-us.org.

description: Attachment 1: Combined Synopsis-Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services Description This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with the format Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) subpart 12.202, Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The Louis Stokes VA Medical Center in Cleveland, OH, is seeking a qualified contractor to provide all labor, materials, transportation, and supervision for the annual inspection and testing of 18 Cookson Firefly release devices and drop doors. title: 6530--NX EQ Environmental Disinfection Systems Pulsed Xenon UV Light (VA-27-00012571)
description: Sources Sought Notice Sources Sought Notice Page 6 of 6 Sources Sought Notice *= Required Field Sources Sought Notice Page 1 of 6 DESCRIPTION 1.0 DESCRIPTION THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation for bids, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Enterprise Procurement Office (EPO), formerly the Strategic Acquisition Center (SAC), is issuing this Sources Sought Notice as a means of conducting market research to identify qualified sources with the capability and resources to meet the Veterans Health Administration s (VHA) Non-Expendable Equipment National Program requirement for Environmental Disinfection Systems Pulsed Xenon UV Light. The EPO in conjunction with VHA is seeking qualified sources capable of supplying the Xenex LightStrike+ Environmental Disinfection Systems Pulsed Xenon UV Light or equivalent products that satisfy the minimum technical requirements, on an agency-wide basis. VA is contemplating the award of a single Requirements Contract with Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) orders IAW FAR 16.503, Requirements Contracts, to a supplier of this equipment. Respondents will be required to deliver complete Xenex LightStrike+ Environmental Disinfection Systems Pulsed Xenon UV Light to VA medical centers and facilities throughout the United States. The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 334510 Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing and the associated size standard is 1,250 employees. The FAR Provision found at 52.204-7 requires that The Offeror shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer or quotation. You may access the SAM website at SAM.gov | Home. All respondents must be certified with the appropriate NAICS code on the SAM website. All Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) / Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) respondents must be verified in the SBA database at: https://www.sba.gov/veterans/#vetcert at the time of submission. Submissions for this Sources Sought Notice shall be submitted by email no later than November 4, 2026, at 12:00pm Eastern Time to the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer at the following email addresses: Alanna.Wilson@va.gov Anthony.Zibolski@va.gov Email responses shall include the following subject line: Response to Sources Sought Notice 36C10X27Q0009. This notice is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor does the Government intend to pay for any information submitted as a result of this notice. This notice is part of a continuous process for obtaining the latest information on the commercial status of the industry with respect to their current and near-term abilities. The information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for, or award, a competitive contract. It is emphasized that this is a notice solely for planning and informational purposes. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. The Government may or may not issue a solicitation as a result of this notice. There is no solicitation available at this time. 2.0 SCOPE OF WORK The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Non-Expendable Equipment National Program has identified the Environmental Disinfection Systems Pulsed Xenon UV Light as a candidate for a VA-wide (otherwise referred to as national ) contract. Systems that use ultraviolet (UV) light designed to kill, remove, or render inert pathogenic microorganisms present in a closed environment and on hard inanimate surfaces and objects located in that environment (frequently limited to one room). These systems are intended to remove microorganisms from the environment (i.e., most viruses and bacteria, including mycobacteria) and other microbial forms, including spores when using appropriate wavelengths in the UV spectrum. The UV radiation is obtained from dedicated (e.g., low-pressure mercury, pulsed-xenon) lamps that emit radiation in the UV-B and C ranges (e.g., from 200 to 320 nm wavelength); a fixed wavelength of 254 nm is frequently used. The systems are usually automated and include computerized and remote monitoring capabilities. Some systems permit choosing one of several working cycles according to the room disinfection needs. UV environmental disinfection systems are intended for short-term use (e.g., from several minutes to a few hours) in patient rooms, operating rooms, and other healthcare facility closed areas; they are usually used after a terminal cleaning that is performed when a patient is transferred or discharged from a room. The following Contract Line Items (CLINs) are being considered: Contract Line Items Manufacturer Part Number Description 0001 Xenex MXSUV1-FT MXSUV1-FT (Without XCT Program) 0002 Xenex MXSUV1-FTXCT MXSUV1-FT (With XCT Program) 0003 Xenex MXSUV1-SL MXSUV1-SL (Without XCT Program) 0004 Xenex MXSUV1-SLXCT MXSUV1-SLXCT (With XCT Program) 0005 Xenex W W - Optional One Year Warranty Extension Without XCT 0006 Xenex XCTW XCTW - Optional One Year Warranty Extension With XCT Respondents should identify a complete solution including associated accessories, as required for the system s full functionality. The following Minimum Technical Requirements (MTRs) are being considered: FDA Authorized Whole Room Microbial Reduction Devices The contractor shall provide FDA authorized whole room ultraviolet microbial reduction systems. System Architecture Characteristics System shall utilize a high intensity pulsed xenon emitter capable of producing broad spectrum germicidal ultraviolet energy within the 240 315 nm range. System shall operate as a single integrated unit capable of delivering 360-degree germicidal exposure in typical clinical environments. Workflow Characteristics System shall be deployable by a single trained operator. System shall not require staff to reenter the treatment area while cycles are active. System shall support treatment of primary patient care areas as well as adjacent spaces such as restrooms or anterooms through configurable cycle options. Vendor shall provide operator training covering device setup, operation, safety, maintenance, certification, and competency. Technology / Connectivity Characteristics System shall provide a unified operator interface capable of initiating, monitoring, and completing treatment cycles through a single control platform. System shall support cloud-based reporting of cycle completion, operator usage, and device performance analytics. Cloud connectivity features shall function independently of internal facility networks, avoiding reliance on local security credentials or firewalls. Physical / Deployment Characteristics System shall consist of a single mobile unit that can be transported between rooms by one operator. System shall include integrated power management and charging capabilities suitable for frequent deployment within clinical workflows. System shall include durable wheels, handles, and stabilization features appropriate for movement throughout healthcare facilities. System shall be designed for operation in unoccupied clinical rooms, including patient care areas, operating rooms, procedural suites, and utility spaces. For each product identified in the response (brand name and part number), the response must include descriptive literature demonstrating that the product meets or exceeds the MTRs specified above. The Government's intent is to include all ancillary items necessary to ensure the equipment can function as designed by the OEM and as required. Respondents are encouraged to identify any additional accessories, service, or configuration that may be necessary or beneficial to the function

Statement of Work (SOW) For GEC Targeted Adeno Associated Virus Vector Development Contract Description: Development and production of a kidney glomerular endothelial cell specific AAV vector for VA preclinical research. 1.0 Scope of Work: 1.1 This requirement is a VA ORD Merit funded project (#1I21RD001234-01) to develop a kidney glomerular endothelial cell specific viral vector. 1.2 The goal of the project is to build a homing peptide enabled vector platform capable of targeting the glomerular endothelium to treat kidney injury and disease and to enhance traditional pharmacologic approaches. 1.3 The work will modify the capsid of an endothelial specific, non immunogenic viral vector by incorporating a peptide that specifically targets kidney glomerular endothelial cells (GEC), with the objective of increasing specificity, reducing off target transduction, and overcoming known limitations in vector targeting to the kidney. 2.0 Background: 2.1 This requirement in response to RD-01-PILT: ISRM Pilot Project Award I21 was selected for funding by ORD; Merit funded project (1I21RD001234-01). 2.2 Despite aggressive management of blood pressure and glycemic control, the prevalence of kidney disease continues to rise, highlighting the need for adjunctive, individualized approaches that advance precision medicine. The project aims to build a homing peptide enabled vector platform targeting the glomerular endothelium to treat kidney injury and disease and to augment current therapeutic strategies. 2.3 Effective vector targeting of the kidney is impeded by the filtering function of the glomerulus and the risk of off target transduction, which may cause adverse effects. These challenges are compounded by the complex architecture of the kidney. Phage enabled peptide homing provides a powerful tool to refine tissue and cell specificity. Developing a targeted vector for GECs cells central to kidney disease development has strong potential to increase selectivity and minimize off target effects. 2.4 To address this need, the requirement leverages two technologies: (1) Biopanning with phage display to select peptides that specifically target kidney glomerular endothelial cells, and (2) capsid modification of an endothelial specific, non immunogenic vector to improve specificity and reduce off target transduction. 2.5 The services required will: 2.5.1 Validate a GEC targeting peptide and incorporate it into an endothelial specific adeno associated virus (AAV) capsid to control transduction specificity. 2.5.1.1Aim 1 refines phage display selection between murine and human renal versus extra renal endothelial cells to confirm GEC selectivity, followed by incorporation into the AAV capsid 2.5.2 Test the feasibility of the GEC specific AAV vector in culture studies (binding and internalization) and in vivo (biodistribution and transduction efficacy). 2.5.1.2 Aim 2 evaluates the targeting peptide modified AAV vector in murine kidney slices and in vivo biodistribution studies, followed by ex vivo immunofluorescent validation. The vector will also be tested in a murine model of endothelial glomerular filtration barrier injury. 2.6 This requirement will overcome current limitations in kidney specific vector targeting caused by the organ s complex cellular architecture and will create a clinically translatable cell specific vector platform designed to reduce off target effects. 3.0 Technical Requirements/Tasks: 3.1 Within one year of the start date of the funding award. The contractor shall independently perform all technical tasks required to engineer, produce, and validate a kidney glomerular endothelial cell (GEC) specific viral vector. Task one will require a high level of demonstrated proficiency and efficiency to be able to complete within one year. 3.1.1 Task 1: Peptide Incorporation Into Viral Capsid 3.1.1.1 Identified targeting peptides shall be engineered by the contractor into the AAV VP1 capsid at amino acid position 588/589, a well tolerated insertion site. 3.1.1.2 Modified AAV viruses will be produced serially. 3.1.1.3 Verified GEC peptide+AAV capsid plasmids will be used to generate vectors containing an eGFP reporter for quantitative assessment of vector function. 3.1.1.4 Specificity and transduction efficiency will be evaluated across a panel of cell types using flow cytometry. 3.1.1.5 Peptide robustness will be evaluated through iterative comparisons of peptide alone versus peptide displayed on the AAV6 capsid. 3.1.1.6 Fluorescent peptide binding to a biomarker unique to GEC will be quantified (KD, IC50) to confirm specificity. 3.1.1.7 Task one will be considered complete when peptide sequencing is completed in accordance with the research protocol. Receipt of the data readout and a satisfactory progress report that outlines the data and any needed adaptations for the next tasks by end of funding period one will complete the task 3.1.2 Task 2: Will begin once there is satisfactory completion of task one. Testing of GEC Specific Peptide Vector Binding will be performed independently by the contractor beginning at the start of the second funding period and must be complete by the end of the second year of the award 3.1.2.1 Supernatant containing the GEC peptide+vector will be incubated with cultured murine kidney tissue slices to assess binding and internalization. 3.1.2.2 Round 1 panning will use laser capture microdissection to collect GEC bound phage. 3.1.2.3 Rounds 2 and 3 will refine targeting using mixed kidney derived cell populations and control tissues. 3.1.2.4 Uptake in non target cells (e.g., hepatocytes, AEC, RECs) will be collected for analysis of non specific binding. 3.1.2.5 Task two will be considered complete when the results of the testing of the GEC-Specific Peptide Vector Binding are submitted to the research team for review and analysis and deemed acceptable. If revision work is needed that will occur in conjunction with Task 3. Completion of this task will require satisfactory progress report that outlines the data and any needed adaptation for the next task. 3.1.3 Task 3: Specificity and Efficiency Testing of the Modified Vector 3.1.3.1 Bioluminescence imaging will be performed over a time course using luciferase reporter constructs to quantify transduction efficiency and determine optimal timepoints. 3.1.3.2 Renal artery infusion of the GEC peptide modified AAV (or control AAV) will be performed to assess target and off target accumulation. 3.1.3.3 Ex vivo whole organ imaging (IVIS Spectrum) and immunohistochemistry/immunofluorescence will confirm organ and cellular level distribution. 3.1.3.4 Vector genome presence will be assessed by AAV ITR specific PCR. 3.1.3.5 Tissue and plasma samples will be collected to evaluate kidney function and possible off target effects. 3.1.3.6 Task three will be considered complete when the research team and facility have determined the data report from the efficiency testing are acceptable and a final report outlining all data, interpretations of the data and conclusions and by the end of the second year of the award. 3.1.3.7 Reported data will be generated and sent to the Primary Investigator by the end of each funding period as outlined in the tasks above. 3.2 Other requirements 3.2.1 Quarterly reporting 3.2.1.1 From date of award onward the awardee shall provide quarterly reports verifying what tasks were completed, current stage and any recent or pending results in alignment with the three tasks 3.1.1, 3.1.2, and 3.1.3 from the VA ORD Merit funded project (#1I21RD001234-

title: Earned Wage Access
description: Request for Information # 70T01027I7663N001 Earned Wage Access Services 1. Purpose The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to conduct market research on commercially available Earned Wage Access (EWA) services and to identify capable vendors that may be able to provide a secure, fully managed EWA solution for eligible TSA employees. Information received will support acquisition planning, help TSA assess industry capabilities and implementation approaches, and inform the development of any future solicitation. This RFI is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by the Government. 2. Anticipated Scope TSA anticipates seeking a Contractor to provide, operate, maintain, and support a voluntary EWA platform for eligible TSA employees. The anticipated service includes secure integration with TSA�s designated Federal payroll provider, employee enrollment and identity verification, earned-wage balance calculation, employee fund-transfer options, customer support, platform maintenance, security and compliance reporting, and program management. The attached draft Performance Work Statement provides additional detail regarding the anticipated scope and requirements. 3. Background TSA employs a geographically dispersed workforce across the United States and U.S. territories. TSA Human Capital is exploring EWA as a potential voluntary employee service to support financial readiness and stability by enabling employees to access a portion of wages they have already earned before the standard biweekly Federal payroll date. The intended service would offer an alternative to high-cost lending products, credit cards, or emergency loans, while preserving the integrity of official Federal payroll processes and avoiding direct costs to the U.S. Government. 4. Period and Place of Performance TSA anticipates that any resulting contract may include a one-year base period with subsequent option periods; however, the final period of performance and contract structure will be determined through acquisition planning. Performance is expected to occur primarily at Contractor facilities and in Contractor-hosted cloud environments, with services supporting TSA employees located throughout all U.S. States and U.S. territories. The Contractor may be required to participate in virtual or in-person meetings with TSA personnel as directed by the Government. 5. Performance Outcomes and Objectives The anticipated EWA service should provide eligible, voluntarily enrolled TSA employees with a secure, reliable, and accessible means to access earned but unpaid wages between regular pay cycles. The Contractor should deliver a highly available platform; protect employee and Government information; provide transparent fee disclosures; maintain employee support services; and ensure the solution does not disrupt, alter, or delay official Federal payroll operations. The Contractor will also be expected to maintain appropriate financial capacity, assume responsibility for EWA transactions, provide meaningful performance reporting, and support service continuity during Federal Government shutdowns. 6. Transition TSA does not currently have an existing contract for EWA services. Therefore, any future Contractor would be responsible for transition-in activities necessary to establish a new EWA capability, including implementation planning, coordination with TSA and the designated payroll provider, secure integration and testing, operational readiness activities, and support for employee launch communications as directed by TSA. The Contractor would also be expected to provide transition-out support at the conclusion of the contract or upon Government direction, including secure transfer of Government data and records, continuity coordination, knowledge transfer, and disposition or sanitization of Government Furnished Information, as applicable. 7. Performance Constraints The anticipated service must be provided at no direct cost to the U.S. Government and must not interfere with official Federal payroll processing. The Contractor will be expected to meet applicable Federal security, privacy, accessibility, and records-management requirements, including use of a FedRAMP-authorized environment as applicable and conformance with Section 508 requirements for information and communications technology. The Contractor must assume sole financial and legal responsibility for EWA funds and transactions, maintain transparent employee fee disclosures, support employees nationwide and in U.S. territories, and demonstrate the capability to continue EWA operations during a partial or full Federal Government shutdown in accordance with the attached PWS. 8. Responses to the RFI Should Include Cover Letter, One-Page Limit: Interested parties should provide a one-page cover letter that identifies the company�s legal name, business address, Unique Entity Identifier, if available, business size and socioeconomic status, primary point of contact, NAICS codes and applicable Federal contract vehicles. The letter should briefly state the organization�s interest in the requirement and indicate whether the organization anticipates serving as a prime contractor or through a teaming arrangement. Capabilities Statement, Five-Page Limit: Interested parties should submit a capabilities statement describing their ability to meet the anticipated EWA requirement described in the attached PWS. The capabilities statement should summarize the organization�s EWA platform and employee-support capabilities; relevant experience with Federal or similarly regulated payroll-system integrations; FedRAMP, security, privacy, and Section 508 capabilities; financial capacity to fund wage advances; approach to transaction liability and Government-shutdown continuity; comparable past performance; anticipated implementation approach and timeline; and ability to provide performance reporting, transition support, and transparent employee fee disclosures. Respondents may also identify recommended refinements or considerations for TSA�s future acquisition approach. Responses to Government Questions, No Page Limit: In addition to the cover letter and capabilities statement, interested parties should provide concise responses to the following questions. Responses may be included as an attachment and should identify the corresponding question number. Should earned wages be calculated using official time and attendance data? Please describe the recommended approach and rationale. How does the respondent recommend receiving employee salary, pay-rate, and hours-worked information? What cadence does the respondent recommend for receiving salary, pay-rate, and time-and-attendance data files? What controls would the contractor use to prevent employee disbursements from exceeding actual available net pay? How would corrections, retroactive adjustments, late timecard changes, leave-without-pay, and other no-pay situations be handled? How would debt collection be handled if an overpayment occurs? How would the contractor ensure that the service does not interfere with statutory deductions, including court-ordered deductions, tax liens, or other payroll obligations? Would there be a cutoff time or cutoff date for daily payments within each pay period? If so, please describe. How would the contractor�s process align with the NFC payroll-processing cycle, pay-period closeout, and official pay day? How would pay reconciliation occur each pay period between contractor disbursements and NFC payroll? In the event of a lapse in appropriations or Federal Government shutdown, how would pay availability be calculated if current payroll or time-and-attendance transmissions are unavailable or delayed?
